dedupe_keys.name: open rigbi open data risk analysis of global mobile broadband infrastructure

description: open-rigbi is the code base behind a global assessment of the vulnerability of mobile telecommunications infrastructure to climate hazards. It takes base station locations from the crowdsourced OpenCelliD database and hazard layers for coastal flooding, river flooding and tropical cyclones, preprocesses boundaries and hazard rasters country by country, intersects cells with hazard footprints for each return period and climate scenario, applies damage assumptions to estimate direct costs, and produces the figures, cost maps and validation of flooded areas used in the paper. It was written by Edward Oughton with Tom Russell and Jim Hall of the University of Oxford and World Bank colleagues, first posted on arXiv in 2023 and published in Nature Communications in 2026. Coverage: global, country by country, historical and RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios. Format and access: Python and R scripts with a conda environment file on GitHub; input data on Zenodo; free under the MIT licence. Caveats: running the whole pipeline needs large global hazard rasters and the OpenCelliD extract; damage functions are simple; the README focuses on regenerating figures. Simulation uses: hazard exposure and direct damage of telecom networks, adaptation screening and inputs to cross-sector risk models. Related records: its results are published as a separate Zenodo dataset, OpenCelliD provides assets, and the Lights Out study treats fibre and nodes under sea level rise.
